title: NO surface anywhere answers 'what roster has the running trader actually loaded' — every one of them re-reads the YAML
note:
DONE 2026-09-24 -- merged AND observed. OBSERVED 2026-09-24T06:34:28Z. GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/runtime-config (the served twin of scripts/ops/verify_running_roster.py, both shipped by #12738) returned HTTP 200 with process_state `observed`, verdict CURRENT, and reload_state `current` for BOTH accounts_yaml and strategies_yaml -- loaded_digest == on_disk_digest (accounts sha256:797eca02..., strategies sha256:2669a35d...). pid 4137367, boot 2026-09-24T06:25:27Z, last_tick 06:34:20Z, tick_age 8.1s, bot_ticking true, git_sha f8ef1db5b. f8ef1db5b contains a66a1eca2 (#12738) -- checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, not assumed. The restart came from system-action `pull-and-deploy` (issue #12797, run 35964326891, wrapper exit 0): HEAD f7a052513 -> f8ef1db5b, ict-trader-live.service and ict-web-api.service both bounced at 06:25:28Z.

The endpoint answering at all is itself the deploy evidence: /api/bot/runtime-config did not exist before a66a1eca2, so a 200 from it cannot be returned by the pre-merge code. What the row asked for is now true: a surface reports the roster the RUNNING PROCESS holds, stamped by the loaders at load time, separately from the files on disk.

PRIOR NOTE ----------------------------------------------------------------
BUILT 2026-09-22, PR #12738 (draft, Tier-2 hold). THE ROW'S DIAGNOSIS WAS RE-VERIFIED FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN TRUSTED, and it was right on all three counts: /api/bot/config's field is `yaml_mode`; build_status computes `live` as _read_live_per_account(accounts_yaml) and `strategies` as _read_strategy_names(strategies_yaml), both of which open and parse the YAML. [!] ONE THING THE ROW DID NOT SAY, AND IT CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: what the process holds is ASYMMETRIC. MEASURED 2026-09-22 by reading src/strategy_registry.py, src/runtime/pipeline.py:364, src/units/accounts/__init__.py and src/core/coordinator.py:2795 -- strategy_registry._cache is populated on the first load and NEVER invalidated, and pipeline.STRATEGY_ROSTER resolves at IMPORT, so strategies.yaml needs a RESTART; load_accounts() re-opens accounts.yaml on every call (once per tick via main._resolve_tick_symbols, once per dispatch via multi_account_execute), so that half converges on the next tick. A single `is it current?` boolean would have been wrong for one of them, so the surface reports PER FILE. [!] WHAT SHIPPED: src/runtime/loaded_config.py (producer; two three-state contracts now registered with collapsed-state-guard, which is clean at 50) -- `process_state` observed/not_written/unreadable keeps `we could not look` out of `the trader holds nothing` (`loaded` is null, never []), and `reload_state` current/pending_reload/unknown is the field that turns `deployed` into an observation. Each loader stamps the path, a sha256 over THE EXACT BYTES IT PARSED, a UTC timestamp, and the values it resolved (per-account dry_run read off the RiskManager the process built, never re-derived from the file). runtime_status.json gains a `process` block; schema_version stays 1 because the addition is additive and the reader detects it by PRESENCE. Served at GET /api/bot/runtime-config (Tier 1, read-only) and by scripts/ops/verify_running_roster.py. [!] THE THREE FALSE CLAIMS ARE CORRECTED IN PLACE AND THE CAPABILITY WAS BUILT RATHER THAN THE CLAIM DELETED, as the row required -- and there was a THIRD the row did not name: /api/bot/strategies' `loaded` column was documented as `the names the running process actually loaded` and is a file read. It keeps its meaning (the SPA consumes it) and gains a tri-state `held_by_process` beside it, where None is not False. [!] VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE DATA, not only fixtures: vm-diag-snapshot relay, issue #12734 / run 35729811659, captured 2026-09-22T12:52:33Z -- the live artifact carries schema_version 1 and NO `process` key, and fed to the new reader it returns `not_written` with `loaded: None`. That is a live positive control for the state that matters most. [!] READ-ONLY AND FENCED: the stamp inside load_accounts is reached from Coordinator.multi_account_execute and is wrapped so a failure to OBSERVE degrades to `no stamp` and dispatch continues byte-for-byte. Nothing in the order path consults any of it, and nothing may be made to. FOUND 2026-09-22 by the manager at close-out, while trying to establish what would move R2 and B2 from `landed_unproven` to `done`. It turns out nothing can, today. [!] READ FROM THE CODE, NOT THE PROSE. (1) /api/bot/config's per-account mode field is literally named `yaml_mode` -- honest naming, and it means the payload reports the FILE on the VM. (2) The payload's `trading_mode` block carries a note asserting `live_per_account is the pipeline's runtime view`, which is STRONGER THAN WHAT THE CODE DOES: that value comes from runtime_status.json, written by the live pipeline on every tick via src/web/runtime_status.py::build_status -- and build_status computes it as `_read_live_per_account(accounts_yaml)`, which OPENS AND PARSES config/accounts.yaml. (3) The same file's `strategies` field is `_read_strategy_names(strategies_yaml)`, which opens and parses config/strategies.yaml. [!] SO THE ONE ARTIFACT THE TRADING PROCESS ITSELF WRITES REPORTS THE CONFIG FILE, NOT ITS OWN LOADED STATE. `the pipeline wrote it` is not `the pipeline is using it`, and every reader has been taking the first for the second. The genuine process facts in that file are bot_uptime_s and git_sha; the roster and the per-account mode are not among them. [!] WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY, ON A LIVE-MONEY SYSTEM: a roster edit is not live until the trader reloads config. Between the merge and that reload, a leg the evidence bar just CUT is still trading real money, and there is no way to tell -- every surface shows the cut. R2 (Tier-3, 4 legs cut from bybit_2 / bybit_portfolio / breakout_1) and B2 (alpaca_portfolio 14 -> 2) are both `landed_unproven` for exactly this reason, and both would close the moment such a surface existed. Same defect class as E22: a reading surface structurally unable to express the state that matters. [!] DELIVERABLE: make runtime_status.json (or a sibling) report the roster the process HOLDS -- pipeline.STRATEGIES and the resolved per-account effective_dry -- beside the file-read values, with the two DISTINGUISHABLE and a `config_reloaded_at` stamp so `pending_reload` is a readable state rather than an invisible one. Then fix /api/bot/config's note, which currently claims a runtime view it does not have. Tier 2: it changes what a live service publishes. [!] DO NOT `fix` this by deleting the note and leaving the gap -- the note is wrong because the capability is missing, not the other way round. [!] CLOSE-OUT TRUE-STATE PASS, 2026-09-22T18:4xZ, manager session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH. Was `queued` with no PR link while #12738 sat finished. This row reaches `done` only when scripts/ops/verify_running_roster.py reports reload_state `current` for accounts_yaml ON THE VM after the restart - merged is not deployed and deployed is not observed. [!] OPERATOR APPROVAL GIVEN 2026-09-24, and this edge is cleared on that basis rather than on a re-reading of this row. Asked as one of four decisions, naming in terms that merging IS the VM mutation and is the only thing that converts the ada_pullback_2h promotion from merged to OBSERVED; the operator chose 'Approve - merge, restart, verify' over both 'merge only, no restart' and 'hold'. So the approval covers the DEPLOY. [!] THIS ROW STILL DOES NOT REACH `done` ON THE MERGE. Sequence the manager owes: merge -> ~5 min for ict-git-sync -> restart ict-trader-live via the system-actions allowlist -> scripts/ops/verify_running_roster.py must report reload_state `current` for accounts_yaml ON THE VM. Merged is not deployed and deployed is not observed; only that last reading closes it, and it also closes R2 and B2.
